question: Why do they experiment with RNNs instead of transformers for this task?
title: Combating Adversarial Misspellings with Robust Word Recognition
answer_short: Because character-level and word-piece models are more vulnerable to adversarial attacks due to finer-grained manipulations.
answer_rationale: The document explains that although one might intuitively expect word-piece and character-level models to be more robust to adversarial attacks due to context usage, experiments show they are actually more vulnerable. This is because each character-level edit in these models produces a distinct input, giving attackers more options to exploit, compared to word-level models which are mostly limited to UNK-ing words. This vulnerability is explicitly discussed in Text 1 and Text 7, which highlight the sensitivity and attack surface differences between model types.
